passage: Reena stood at the sofa. First she scrambled belly-first and slid off. Then she stopped. "Knee!" she said, remembering the one that worked, and swung a knee onto the cushion edge, then the other leg over. Charu, Reena's mother, counted quietly. By the next evening Reena started every climb with the knee, and each time she was quicker than before.

qa.q: How did Reena start every climb by the next evening?
qa.a: Reena started every climb with the knee on the cushion edge.

qa.q: What was Reena feeling when saying "Knee!"?
qa.a: Reena was confident and pleased, because she remembered a move that had worked and chose it. 🙂

qa.q: What could Reena try if the knee move does not work on a taller seat, and why?
qa.a: Reena could test a new way, like using a low stool or asking Charu, because a move that worked on one sofa might not fit another height.

qa.q: How does Charu see Reena's method?
qa.a: Charu sees Reena improving with practice, which is why Charu counts quietly and lets the climbing continue.

grounding: A toddler starts each sofa climb with a knee on the cushion edge, having found that it helped, and gets steadily faster.

passage:
"Watch, Francis mama," Bhupen's mother said. "Bhupen, show him."
Bhupen marched to the sofa, planted a knee on the seat's edge and pushed. Up.
"Wah!" said Francis mama. "How did he learn that?"
"Last week the knee worked once. Now it's always the knee."
"Down, and again!" Bhupen slid off, knee up, push. Up. Faster than before.
"He's timing himself," Francis mama laughed.

qa.q: What did Bhupen plant on the seat's edge?
qa.a: He planted a knee on the seat's edge.

qa.q: What was Bhupen feeling as he slid off to go again?
qa.a: He was proud and excited, eager to show off his fast climb.

qa.q: What else could Bhupen's mother try to keep him learning?
qa.a: She could offer a different sofa or a higher chair with her nearby, so he tests whether the knee trick works elsewhere.

qa.q: How does Francis mama see the climbing?
qa.a: He is impressed and amused, laughing that Bhupen seems to be timing himself.

grounding: A toddler starts every sofa climb with the knee that worked before and gets faster each time.

passage:
Crèche note, Monday
Pankaj has found his way onto the reading couch. Last Friday he got up by pressing one knee on the couch's front edge. Today, every time, he began the same way: knee first, push, roll in. By the fourth time he was up in a few seconds. His father, Santosh, arrived at pickup and watched him do it twice, smiling. I stood beside the couch each time.

qa.q: What did Pankaj do first every time today?
qa.a: He began the same way: knee first, push, roll in.

qa.q: How can you tell Pankaj felt confident?
qa.a: He climbed straight up every time without hesitating and got faster, by the fourth time taking only a few seconds.

qa.q: What small step could the note-writer try next?
qa.a: They could offer a slightly different couch or step with them standing beside it, so Pankaj practises adapting his knee move.
Santosh seems pleased and proud, smiling as he watches his son climb twice.

grounding: A crèche note records a toddler who repeats the knee-first climb that worked before and gets faster each time.
